name: Shaker
summary: The rooms of the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing in New England, New York and Kentucky. Built-in storage, a peg rail around the walls, light wood furniture and bare floor give a room that is ordered for work and easy to clean.

philosophy.core_thesis: A room is beautiful when each object in it is useful, well made and in its place.
design_principles: Build the storage into the wall: one case of drawers and cupboards from floor to ceiling on one wall, with no free-standing chests.
Run a peg rail around the room at 180–190 cm above the floor, with a turned peg each 30 cm, and hang chairs, clothes and tools on it.
Place doors, windows and pairs of furniture in mirror pairs about the centre line of the room.
Leave 70–80% of the floor bare, so that the floor is easy to sweep.
Use one wood species and one paint colour for all woodwork in a room.
Make each drawer in a case 10–15% taller than the drawer above it.
Keep each piece light: a ladder-back chair weighs 4–5 kg and one person can lift it onto the peg rail.
anti_patterns: Carved, gilded or veneered ornament on furniture or trim
Hung pictures, mirrors with frames or display shelves of ornaments
Heavy upholstered sofas and armchairs that stay on the floor
Furniture placed at an angle to the walls
More than one accent paint colour in one room

composition.plan_logic: An orthogonal room with one centre line. Built-in storage fills one wall, and furniture stands parallel to the other walls.
composition.focal_point: The built-in wall of drawers and cupboards on the centre line, or a cast-iron stove on the axis in front of it.

rules.rule: Make the built-in case the single focal point. Hang nothing above it and put nothing in front of it.
Put the door, the windows and each pair of beds or chairs in mirror pairs about the centre line.
Run the peg rail at one height around the full room, and space the pegs equally.
Graduate the drawers of a case from the top down.
Keep chairs and tables light and slender: legs of 3–4 cm section, seats at chair height.
Keep the centre of the floor empty. Hang the chairs on the rail when the room is not in use.
Show two planes only: the furniture against the walls, and the walls themselves.
Give each room one use. Put the work, rest and storage zones along the walls, not in the centre.
Keep a straight clear path from the door to the window.
Align the door with a window in the opposite wall, so that the view from the entrance ends in daylight.
Paint the plaster white or cream. Give the wood and the painted built-ins the secondary share, and one accent paint to a door or a box.
Light the room by day from two walls of sash windows. After dark, use one low ambient layer and one task lamp at the work table.
Use one wood species and one woodwork colour per room. The only deviation is the accent paint.
Shoot the room level, with a one-point view square to the built-in wall from the door on the centre line.

zoning.circulation: One straight route from the door to the window, and a perimeter band of 70 cm in front of the built-ins and the peg rail.

palette.distribution: White or cream plaster on walls and ceiling; honey wood on floor and furniture; one painted colour on all woodwork; one accent on a door, a box or a cupboard.

colours.name: Red ochre
colours.surface: one door or one oval box

lighting.strategy: Daylight is the main light. After dark, a few small sources at table height give a low, even light without a centre fixture.
lighting.daylight: Tall double-hung sash windows of 12 over 12 panes in two walls. White walls spread the light; window glass is 15–20% of the floor area.

layers.position: on the peg rail, 2 per wall

materials.finish: Thin oil, shellac or milk paint at a matt to satin sheen. No veneer, no gilding, no varnish build-up.
materials.texture_contrast: Planed wood against matt plaster, at close to 1:1. The woven tape seat is the only coarse texture.

furniture.silhouette: Slender turned posts and tapered legs. Ladder-back chairs with 3 or 4 arched slats; tables with plain aprons and no stretchers in view.
furniture.arrangement: Each piece stands against a wall and parallel to it. Chairs hang upside down on the peg rail when the floor is cleaned.

textiles.pattern: Plain cloth, checks and stripes in one or two colours. Chair tapes weave a checkerboard of two colours.
textiles.windows: Plain roller blinds or short cotton curtains on a rod inside the frame. The window frame stays visible.

objects.approach: Only useful objects are on show: boxes, baskets, brooms and tools hang on the rail or stand on a shelf.
objects.grouping: Oval boxes stand in graduated stacks of 3 to 5. Tools and clothes hang in one row on the peg rail.

implementation.brief: A plain room of white plaster and honey wood. One wall is a built-in case of graduated drawers; a peg rail runs around the room; two ladder-back chairs and a table stand against the walls.
implementation.image_prompt: Shaker interior, symmetrical room, white lime plaster walls, built-in cherry case of graduated drawers on the back wall, blue-painted peg rail at head height around the room, ladder-back chairs hung on the rail, wide pine floorboards, bare floor, tall twelve-over-twelve sash windows, soft north daylight, no decoration, documentary photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Carved ornament, sofa, rug pattern, framed pictures, mirrors, clutter, chrome, plastic, coloured light, gloss.
implementation.camera: 35 mm lens, camera at 150 cm, one-point view square to the built-in wall from the door on the centre line.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 500 x 400 cm, ceiling 270 cm. Sun and sky through two sash windows in the side walls; one 2200 K point light at 75 cm on the table for night.

lineage.root: It came from the rules of a religious community and from plain country joinery, and neither has a style record in the data.

emotion.target_response: Calm order: the viewer sees that everything has a place and that the room asks for nothing more.

avoid_when: The brief asks for display, luxury or status.
The room must hold a large collection of objects on show.

modifiers.how: Change the wood to pale oak, add a wool rug, a sofa and 3–5 small lamps; keep the bare walls and the single focal wall.
Lower the furniture to 38 cm seats, remove the peg rail, and add one stoneware vessel; keep one wood and the bare floor.
